mia: heads-up - noticed a regression after yesterday's kernel-picker change on canary. p95 up ~18%, tokens/s down ~30%. dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/c/anom
oliver: saw the alert, thanks. which workload? long-tail seqs or short prompts?
devon: spotted it on streaming chat workload (avg len 120, tail 800). I ran a quick nsight pass.
mia: baseline (before change) p50=45ms p95=120ms tokens/s=45k. canary after change p50=48ms p95=142ms tokens/s=32k.
oliver: rough hypothesis: picker is favoring smaller-kernel matmul for many small batches, but when we get variable seqs it fragments and causes extra H2D copies / stream syncs.devon: ran nsys + perfetto dump. command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt,osrt:memcpy -o /tmp/canary_run nsys ./run_workload.sh --seq-dist longtail
```
nsys output highlights:
- lots of small `matmul_small_k` launches (~120x) at ~2.3ms each
- fewer `matmul_large_k` launches (~30x) at ~0.7ms each
- host->device memcpy spikes interleaved, ~0.4-0.7ms
- CUDA stream priority flips visible in timeline (low-prio compute queues preempted by memcpy)

perfetto flame snapshot link: https://perfetto/redwood/trace/abc123

mia: any obvious kernel hot spots? devon: hotspot shows kernel selection heuristic picked low-occupancy kernels when batch window < 4 but with KV cache restores the effective work per batch varies -> fragmentation. also observed stream priority inversion: memcpy scheduled on high-prio stream, compute on low-prio -> compute stalls.
oliver: interesting. so two interacting issues: (1) kernel choice threshold too aggressive for small-batch pattern, (2) memcpy/stream priority causing preempt.

devon: quick numbers from trace (rough):
- compute-only time increased from 180ms -> 210ms
- queue-to-execute gaps increased from 12ms -> 38ms (p95)
- extra memcpy overhead ~+18ms total across trace
- end-to-end p95 aligned with those extra gaps

mia: this matches the customer repro. can we reproduce locally with a reduced harness?
devon: yes, I made a small harness that simulates KV cache hit pattern + long-tail tokens. runs attached in gist: https://gist/redwood/harness

oliver: proposed fix options:
- raise threshold so that for variable seqs we pick `matmul_large_k` if expected compute > X tokens
- enforce compute streams at high priority or move memcpys to low priority background stream
- add a short batching-delay when tail variance > threshold to form stable batches

mia: which is lowest-risk to try on canary first?
devon: move memcpy to low priority / background stream is easiest and reversible. I can prototype tomorrow and run the same nsys pass.

perf-bot: created perf ticket RWDT-3247 for "picker+stream priority regression - canary 2026-03-17" and attached initial nsys snapshot.

oliver: devon - call out tests to run: replicate canary config, run 3x nsys + perfetto, capture occupancy, kernel counts, and queue gaps. post condensed CSV.

devon: will do. timeline: prototype memcpy-priority flip -> run harness -> post results by EOD tomorrow.
mia: thanks. if memcpy-priority fixes > revert picker change until we have a more nuanced heuristic.

oliver: noted. also add a small telemetry flag to record kernel-choice reason in production traces (`picker.v=reason`) so we can correlate in future.
devon: added to todo. I'll include sample nvtx markers in next trace so we can filter.
mia: :thumbsup: good plan — keep thread updated with artifacts.
